correctness.rationale: The renewal transform for Poisson-reset Brownian first passage and exponential-death conditioning gives exact dimensionless mean M and variance V. Their difference V−M² has the sign of B(sqrt(m+rho))−m. Exact derivative identities and the all-n coefficient argument show that B has one and only one positive maximum, above 1 and below z_c². Restricting crossings to rho>0 and tracking z>sqrt(m) yields precisely 1,1,2,1,0 positive intersections in the five mortality regimes; the equality is tangential at m=m_c. An independent standard-library program verifies the identities and source moment equations, but the infinite sign and global count rest on the written analytic proof.

evidence: Radice, arXiv:2211.16173: the successful-hitting-time Laplace transform and its conditional mean and variance are already given in Eqs. (71)-(72).

The original paper discusses a single equality rate and an approximate existence threshold in its graphical presentation, not a proof that the equality curve has a global maximum and exactly two positive roots for mortality between 1 and 1.1064282209364.

The new proof differentiates the published transform, finds an explicit exponential-polynomial derivative, proves exactly one positive derivative zero by an infinite coefficient sign argument, then enforces the physical constraint z>sqrt(m).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The baseline mean/variance formulas imply the claim only after substantial additional analytic sign/physical-domain analysis; the published statement does not directly assert either the reentrant interval or the sharp global count. As an explicit refinement deducible from known formulas, implicit coverage remains the strongest unresolved publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: Conditional hitting-time variability in mortal search is a physical reliability observable. The existing numerical study treats the unit-CV rate as a single value near a death-threshold; the theorem rigorously discovers and completely characterizes a nonempty interval in which two distinct positive reset rates separately achieve unit CV, with a strict below/above/below sign sequence. It determines the exact universal threshold and tangency and scales to arbitrary diffusivity and target distance. It does not claim broader reset protocols or other optimization objectives.
